The new fixture lib/tests/fixtures/jbmc-defects/F.java has one void method per part of the JVM's semantics for such an initializer (JVMS 5.5: the exception wrapped in ExceptionInInitializerError, the class erroneous with NoClassDefFoundError at the next use, the initializer run once, an Error passed through unwrapped), plus copies of the two corpus methods. It tells JBMC's semantics from a flag or the adapter's reading of the trace. The fixture README and the cleanup-jbmc brief's Progress say so.

### VF-019: --confirm's refusal of a domain JBMC is not given is named, and the confirm conformance test reads it as no verdict

change `uytnkqstzukt` · [log `01bf92755850`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/a8cc612f-0606-4d4c-af9c-ef4ccb4bfee3/01bf92755850780fdc0eebe7d634c30f63a4f1b038bb6c8eb2dbd2961e5c677a.jsonl.gz)

VF-019 (verification/findings.md): under auto --confirm, H2's six nullable and may-alias claims gave 'no engine wrote a harness' in the_corpus_agrees_with_the_jvm_under_auto_confirm (job 20261107-043420), and then 'the corpus says it is refuted, the JVM does not' for the refuted ones. --confirm and --engine jbmc already refused such a domain, with a reason in words, but before writing the harness, so the test had nothing to run on the JVM and could not tell the refusal from a run that went wrong.

property::Outcome gains refused, the name of the rule that refused the property before any checker ran: WIDENED_DOMAIN ('widened-domain', also in prove --json), and None for every other refusal and for any run a checker made. The conformance driver treats a claim with no harness whose every run is Unverifiable and refused by name as no verdict, not judged against the JVM in that test (the test under JBMC and auto, whose plain auto runs write the harness, judges it). Any other missing harness still fails. lib/README.md says the refusal's name.

change `muznwonpkprx` · [log `fb79d60216ea`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/a8cc612f-0606-4d4c-af9c-ef4ccb4bfee3/fb79d60216eabb7ff3d034a744374f88594f801addba5ea779821b88cd5bde65.jsonl.gz)

VF-018: four of H5's ignored heap tests (Kernel#price's output relation, Prices#total's computed equations, Lines#reprice's and Orders#reprice's equations) failed because JBMC did not finish within the tests' own 600 s, the options' default timeout_seconds, while the own checker proves each claim. By the user's decision, the first and only attempt is more time with the expectations unchanged. lib/tests/heap.rs's related_on and property_on now set timeout_seconds from JVMCONTRACT_HEAP_TIME_LIMIT for runs on an engine other than the own checker (600 s when unset; a value that is not a positive number of seconds stops the test, so a job asking for more never silently runs with less). The own checker keeps the default, so the tests that are not ignored are unchanged. heap.rs is a shared file; this only adds to it. Reproducer: the_jbmc_tests_take_their_time_limit_from_the_environment, which doesn't compile without the change. heap's 47 non-ignored tests pass.

Jobs, one per test, each with the variable at 1800 (2 CPUs, 4 GiB, about 70 minutes, a timeout of 100 minutes): 20261107-164356-vf-018-objects-kernel-price-s-output-rel, 20261107-164356-vf-018-prices-prices-total-s-computed-in, 20261107-164356-vf-018-lines-lines-reprice-s-equations-t, 20261107-164356-vf-018-orders-orders-reprice-s-equations.
